main_body: Tall brick shopfront facade: slate mansard roof with two dormers and a chimney, a brick wall with two rows of windows, a balcony rail, and a striped awning over a shop window at the base
top_band: Column at x~20: rows 9-13 grey-teal flat roof band, then rows 14-40 slate roof face (a vertical mansard, not a foreshortened top), then a 3px orange cornice at rows 44-46. No clear top surface sits above the brick body.
evidence: The brick body, which is the largest volume, is drawn straight from the front. The windows, balcony, awning and shop glass are all vertical faces. The only top-like parts are a thin flat teal strip at the roof top and a 2-3px orange cornice, and the slate area reads as a front-facing mansard wall. Unlike the Beodeul houses, whose roofs are big sloped planes seen from above, this roof has no foreshortened surface leading to a front edge. It is a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The brick has individual bricks in several reds plus mortar lines. The slate has course lines and shaded tiles. The lit windows carry speckled warm highlights. Outlines lean to dark brown, teal or slate beside each material rather than pure black. Tile density is comparable to or higher than the references, with only a few small flat patches in the dark balcony and cornice bands.
